features.name: no_comment_uses_first_person_i
features.definition: Is it true that none of the counter-argument comments uses the first-person pronoun "I"?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments with json.loads into a list of strings. If missing/malformed or not a list, return None. If the list is empty, return None. Otherwise, for each comment string, test re.search(r"\bI\b", text) (case-sensitive, standalone capital I; contractions such as I'm, I've, I'd count because the apostrophe is a word boundary; lowercase 'i', 'me', 'my' do not count). Return 1 if no comment matches, else 0. Purely mechanical: quotations, roman numerals, and 'I' inside quoted text are counted too; no semantic filtering.

h0: There is no difference in delta between rows where no counter-argument comment uses \"I\" and rows where at least one does (no_comment_uses_first_person_i has zero association).
h1: Rows where no counter-argument comment uses \"I\" (no_comment_uses_first_person_i = 1) have higher delta (OP view-change) than rows where at least one comment does.
note: Persuasiveness operationalized as the dataset outcome delta (OP changed view). Interpreted "counter-arguments that never use I" as a row-level condition: no available counter-argument comment contains standalone "I". Rows with empty/missing comment lists get null. Mechanical regex also counts "I" in quotations, roman numerals or non-pronoun uses; may be contaminated by outcome-related text in comments; comment timing unknown. Rows with more comments are less likely to satisfy the condition, so comment count is a confound that is not controlled here. Association only, not causal. "Fully impersonal/objective tone" is measured solely by absence of "I", not other personal pronouns.
